explanation: Toggle each letter in a set of odd-frequency letters. A palindrome permits at most one odd frequency.
correctness: Mirrored positions use characters in pairs, leaving at most one center occurrence. Conversely, pairing each even part and placing the possible odd remainder at the center constructs a palindrome.
walkthrough: For aabbc, toggling odd-frequency membership removes a after its second occurrence and removes b after its second. Only c remains odd. It can occupy the middle of a palindrome such as abcba, so return true without enumerating reorderings.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed 26-letter alphabet.
